title: Vision-to-Task Decomposition
summary: A structured worksheet that walks a goal down four levels, from destination to next physical action. Decomposition runs on structure instead of instinct, so nothing depends on a level of detail thinking that drains you.

title: The Pre-Flight Checklist Library
summary: Reusable completeness checklists for the deliverables you produce again and again. Completeness stops depending on memory, the checklist holds the details so you don't have to.

title: The Last 10% Protocol
summary: A defined closing ritual for any deliverable. The hardest part of finishing becomes a checklist, not a judgment call, run in one pass before anything ships.

title: The Detail Debt Log
summary: A running capture list for details consciously deferred in the moment, reviewed on a fixed weekly rhythm. Deferring stops turning into dropping.

title: Timeboxed Detail Sprints
summary: A method for batching detail work into short, scheduled, high-energy blocks. The drain gets contained to windows you chose, instead of leaking across the whole week.

title: The Edge-Case Question Bank
summary: A printed set of boundary-testing questions to run against any plan. You borrow the signature question of the HOW orientation as a tool, without needing the instinct behind it.

title: Definition-of-Done Cards
summary: A card completed at the start of any piece of work that specifies, objectively, what finished means. Done becomes a fact, not a feeling.

title: The Effort Reality-Check
summary: A structured correction for the chronic underestimation of execution effort. The estimate gets built from tasks and history, not from optimism.

title: The AI Precision Companion
summary: A curated prompt pack for delegating precision work to AI: decomposition, checklists, gap reviews, edge cases. The detail thinking gets generated for you, and you stay the judge.

title: The HOW-Partner Review Protocol
summary: A structured way to request a precision review from a HOW-primary colleague. The right partner completes the work, and the protocol makes asking cheap for you and answering easy for them.

title: The Good-Enough Threshold
summary: A worksheet that defines the shipping criteria before work begins. Done becomes a pre-commitment, not an in-the-moment fight against the pull of one more improvement.

title: The Closing Card
summary: An end-of-meeting forcing function: one action, one owner, one date, written before anyone leaves. No conversation ends without becoming movement.

title: The Decision Deadline Ritual
summary: A ritual that timeboxes analysis by setting the decision date in advance. When the date arrives, you decide with the information in hand.

title: The Version 0.5 Reframe
summary: A mental model and a vocabulary for shipping imperfect work as data collection. The early release becomes a method of understanding, which is the register this wiring can genuinely accept.

title: Milestone Backplanning
summary: A template that converts a deep understanding of the work into dated milestones, built backward from the end. The system view becomes a schedule.

title: The WIP Limit Practice
summary: A hard cap on open threads that forces completion before new exploration. Finishing becomes the price of starting, which is the only currency this drain reliably responds to.

title: The Momentum Board
summary: A dead-simple visible tracker of movement, three columns, updated weekly. It externalizes the progress sense your wiring doesn't generate internally.

title: The Progress Broadcast
summary: A fill-in weekly update format, four lines, five minutes. Communicating momentum stops being a writing task and becomes a form.

title: The 48-Hour Draft Rule
summary: A protocol: any new deliverable produces a shareable rough draft within forty-eight hours. Refinement comes after contact, not before.

title: The WHAT-Partner Cadence
summary: A structured pairing with a WHAT-primary who owns pace-setting for a defined piece of work. Momentum becomes someone's energizing job instead of your draining one.

title: The Five-Question Purpose Brief
summary: A ten-minute structured brief, completed once before any significant piece of work begins. It generates the purpose thinking that would otherwise cost you real energy, and captures it in a form you can reference for the life of the project instead of regenerating it every time someone asks.

title: The North Star One-Pager
summary: The purpose of a project, captured once, usually extracted from the person who holds it, and kept visible for its whole life. The why never has to be regenerated mid-flight.

title: The Problem Reframe Deck
summary: A card deck of prompts that pressure-test whether the right problem is being solved. The reframing question gets asked by the cards, so it no longer depends on an instinct that drains you.

title: The So-What Translator
summary: A template that converts detailed output into audience meaning. For every section, one completed sentence: "which means that..." The reader gets significance without you having to feel it first.

title: The Vision Extraction Interview
summary: A structured interview that pulls the vision out of the person who holds it, before execution begins. Purpose gets borrowed from a primary source instead of generated from a drained one.

title: The Quarterly Altitude Check
summary: A scheduled, structured zoom-out: ninety minutes, four questions, once a quarter. Perspective becomes an appointment instead of an instinct you have to summon.

title: The Assumption Audit
summary: A checklist that surfaces the unexamined premises baked into a plan, before execution effort is invested in them. The beliefs get listed, tested, and owned on purpose.

title: The Narrative Arc Template
summary: A five-beat structure that converts detail-rich content into a meaning-led story. The narrative is assembled, not inspired, from material you already have.

title: The Opening Line Habit
summary: A micro-practice: every email, deck, and deliverable opens with one sentence of purpose before any content. Small, trainable, and disproportionate in effect.

title: The Pre-Mortem Protocol
summary: A structured session held before launch: it is twelve months from now, and this failed. Working backward from imagined failure gives systematic thinkers a concrete doorway into strategic thinking.

title: The Energy Budget Planner
summary: A weekly calendar audit that tags work by orientation and rebuilds the schedule around your energy. Tertiary work gets placed at peak hours, in limited doses, with recovery adjacent.

title: The Tertiary Triage Decision Tree
summary: A repeatable decision path for any draining task: scaffold it, timebox it, trade it, or automate it. White-knuckling stops being the default strategy.

title: The Team Trade Board
summary: A team ritual for openly trading work out of tertiaries and into primaries. Under the energy model, a trade is not a favor exchange, it is a net energy gain on both sides.

title: The Drain Signals Field Guide
summary: A guide to recognizing depletion early, in yourself and in teammates. The signals arrive well before the burnout conversation, for those who know what to look for.

title: The Orientation-Balanced Agenda
summary: A meeting agenda template with a segment that serves each orientation, in a deliberate order. No orientation spends the whole meeting drained, and each contributes from its energy.

title: The Three-Question Kickoff
summary: A project kickoff protocol requiring the why, the what, and the how each be answered before work starts. Ten minutes that prevents the three classic mid-project stalls.

title: The Team MindPrint™ Map
summary: A one-page visual of the team's profile composition: where energy concentrates, which orientation is uncovered, and whose role is misloaded. The team's wiring, on one page, in the room.

title: The Friction Forecast
summary: A guide to the predictable friction between orientations, readable from the team map. What looks like a personality clash is usually orientation friction, and friction you can forecast, you can design around.

title: Decision Rights by Orientation
summary: A template that assigns the stages of a decision to the people energized by each stage. Decision load gets matched to cognitive wiring, the way task load already should be.

title: The Mixed-Audience Deck Structure
summary: A presentation architecture for rooms that contain all three orientations. Each wiring hears what it needs to say yes, in the order that keeps everyone in the room.

title: Meeting Keeper Cards
summary: Three rotating meeting roles, purpose keeper, progress keeper, precision keeper, each with a card of licensed interventions. Every orientation's question gets asked, even when its wiring isn't in the room.

title: The Handoff Contract
summary: A short template completed at any cross-orientation handoff: what the receiver needs that the sender wouldn't naturally include, made explicit in both directions.

title: The Team Energy Audit
summary: A quarterly team ritual mapping who is spending sustained time in their tertiary, and why. Structural drain becomes a team agenda item instead of a private endurance test.
